items.title: Roland Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: I said if you really want to get a control and command, play some Scriabin, play some Faure, play some Rachmaninoff, play some Chopin.

ctx.x: Yeah, we were just talking about tributes. Be careful who you pay tribute to. You just were saying some very well thought out phrases about different piano players and I have to say it sounded to me like you were describing yourself.

Oh no, no, no, not me yet. You know I’ll tell you, I’ve worked hard at the piano. I’ve been working almost all my life trying to play the piano. And just when you think you’re getting there, you’re getting to a place where you can do whatever you want to do, something happens that usually you have no control over. And for the last ten, twelve years, I haven’t been able to practice. I’m going to start back. But I haven’t been able to practice. I’ve been working hard and teaching a lot, and there’s no time for me…

explained to him years ago, I can’t even think of how long ago it was but it was more than twenty years ago, I said if you really want to get a control and command, play some Scriabin, play some Faure, play some Rachmaninoff, play some Chopin. Spend time practicing Chopin. They knew what the piano was about. And I told him just like that and he took me to heart. The next thing I know he had a beautiful album out, Faure, Chopin, Rachmaninoff. Yeah it was great, too, to hear that. He took the chords and form and…
